newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in late rebound on speculative buys.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in late rebound on speculative buys.

text.p: Mexican stocks staged a late recovery on Wednesday after sliding for most of the day to close with a toe-hold on positive side.
Traders said the bourse rebounded on selective speculative buying as dealers felt share prices had touched bottom after falling sharply on Monday and Tuesday.
"Late buying in Cemex and Kimber bolstered the IPC as they are blue chips. It didn't take much volume to turn the bourse around," a Mexico City floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 1.92 points, or 0.05 percent, at 3,716.18.
"They snapped up paper towards the close to be ready for when the bourse starts climbing again," the trader added.
Volume was dead slow at just 42.7 million shares traded.
Cement makers Cemex CPO shares gained 50 centavos to 28.70 pesos, while its B shares ended up 35 centavos at 31.80 pesos. Paper company Kimber ended up 0.75 pesos at 32.10 pesos.
The three stocks together accounted for 7.5 percent of all shares traded.
One analyst said he was cautiously optimistic about the outlook for a change in trend on the bourse.

"We are optimistic. Domestic economic fundamentals have not changed and share prices are cheap. We just have to wait until Wall Street settles down before buying," said Alfredo Daz, an equity analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
"Some dealers certainly see a technical rebound in the offing, feel support has been tested and the road is clear to decouple from the Dow Jones," another floor trader said.
The Dow Jones, meanwhile, dropped 1.42 percent to 6,517.01 points.
Sears de Mexico topped the gainers' list
following news Mexican holding company Grupo Carso will buy a 60 percent stake in the retailer from parent company Sears, Roebuck Co.
Sears B1 shares soared 2.64 pesos, or 17.72 percent, to 17.54 pesos, after gaining strongly on Monday and Tuesday amid rumours the Carso deal was about to be settled.

"This is very good for Sears as the economic situation (after the peso devaluation crisis of December 1994) hit the company really hard and Carso has always been hallmarked by successful management," Daz said.
Grupo Carso, meanwhile, gained 35 centavos to 45.15 pesos.

Traders noted the retail sector in general had traded strongly. El Puerto de Liverpool shares ended up 24 centavos at 8.54 pesos, while counterpart Grupo SyR shares were up four centavos to 43 centavos.
Soft drinks firm Jugos del Valle was another prominent gainer, up 24 centavos on news of its launching a Level 1 ADR program.
